items.name: Frame the software as an end-to-end product with a specific outcome and price, not a generic capability.
items.why: A buyer who cannot picture what they get treats the purchase as riskier, so they hesitate or leave.
items.observed: Generic platform pitch: “Intuitive infrastructure to scale any app or agent” with no price or bounded outcome.

items.name: Lead with three key benefits.
items.why: Three claims establish a pattern a reader can act on. A fourth reads as protesting too much and invites scepticism.
items.observed: More than three benefit claims lead, e.g. 'Full-stack previews for every pull request' alongside the h1, so FAIL.
items.citation: When three charms but four alarms (2014)

items.name: Display a strong but imperfect average rating.
items.why: A perfect score reads as curated. A few imperfections are what make the rest credible.
items.observed: No average rating appears; page shows "Trusted by over 6.5 million builders" instead.
